<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Simple linear regression with a polytomous predictor</h1>
  <p>For a categorical predictor with more than two levels, R uses <strong>K − 1</strong> dummy variables. You will fit models, read the coefficients, and change the reference level.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

A <strong>polytomous</strong> predictor has $K > 2$ categories, such as race with three groups or treatment dose with three groups. If the groups are categories, avoid coding them as one numeric variable unless you want to assume a single straight-line trend.

Instead, R picks one <strong>reference</strong> level and creates one dummy variable for each of the other $K - 1$ levels. Each coefficient is that level's mean <strong>difference vs the reference</strong>.

This practical uses datasets available in WebR:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><code>ToothGrowth</code>: tooth length (<code>len</code>) by vitamin C dose (3 levels)</li>
  <li><code>MASS::birthwt</code>: birth weight (<code>bwt</code>) by mother's race (3 levels)</li>
  <li><code>PlantGrowth</code>: plant weight (<code>weight</code>) by treatment group (3 levels)</li>
  <li><code>InsectSprays</code>: insect count (<code>count</code>) by spray type (6 levels)</li>
</ul>

After answering the questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>A categorical predictor with $K = 3$ levels produces how many dummy coefficients (plus the intercept) in a simple regression?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">3 coefficients plus intercept (one per level).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">2 coefficients plus intercept ($K - 1$ dummies).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="c">1 coefficient plus intercept.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. One level is absorbed into the intercept; the other K−1 levels each get a dummy." data-incorrect="Not quite. With K levels, R uses K−1 dummy variables because one level is the reference."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>Why might you convert dose to a factor instead of using one numeric dose column?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">A numeric dose column fits one straight-line trend across the dose levels.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">R cannot read numeric columns.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="c">It removes the intercept from the model.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Treating dose as a factor lets each dose level have its own mean shift vs the reference." data-incorrect="Not quite. The issue is the model assumption, not R's ability to fit numeric predictors."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The equation (three dose levels, 0.5 mg reference)</h2>

<div class="formula-panel">

$$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{dose 1 mg} + b_2 \cdot \text{dose 2 mg}$$

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Each dummy equals 1 only for its own level and 0 otherwise.</li>
  <li>$b_0$ = mean of the <strong>reference</strong> group (0.5 mg dose).</li>
  <li>Each $b_j$ = that level's mean minus the reference mean.</li>
  <li>To recover a group's mean: add its coefficient to the intercept (reference groups add 0).</li>
</ul>

</div>

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 1: tooth length by dose (<code>ToothGrowth</code>)</h2>

The <code>ToothGrowth</code> data record tooth length (<code>len</code>) after three vitamin C dose levels. We treat dose as a factor and set <strong>0.5 mg</strong> as the reference.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: ToothGrowth, 0.5 mg reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(dplyr)
data(ToothGrowth)

tooth <- ToothGrowth |>
  mutate(dose_group = factor(dose,
                             levels = c(0.5, 1, 2),
                             labels = c("dose_0.5", "dose_1", "dose_2")))

mod_dose <- lm(len ~ dose_group, data = tooth)
summary(mod_dose)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>The intercept is about 10.6. This is the mean tooth length for which dose group?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">0.5 mg dose (the reference level).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">2 mg dose.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="c">The average across all three dose groups.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The intercept is always the reference group mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. Look at which level was set as reference when creating the factor."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>The predicted mean tooth length for the <strong>2 mg</strong> dose group is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">15.5 units (the coefficient alone).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">19.7 units (10.6 + 9.1).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="c">26.1 units (10.6 + 15.5).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The 2 mg mean = intercept + dose_groupdose_2 ≈ 10.6 + 15.5 ≈ 26.1." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the 2 mg coefficient to the intercept. The coefficient is a difference, not the full mean."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 5</div>
  <p>The coefficient for <code>dose_groupdose_1</code> (about +9.1) means:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="a">The 1 mg group has mean tooth length 9.1 units in total.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b">The 1 mg group is about 9.1 units <strong>above</strong> the 0.5 mg reference group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="c">The 1 mg group is about 9.1 units above the 2 mg group.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Every dummy coefficient is vs the reference, not vs other non-reference levels." data-incorrect="Not quite. Each row compares that level to the omitted reference (0.5 mg), not to another non-reference level."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 2: birth weight by race (<code>MASS::birthwt</code>)</h2>

The <code>birthwt</code> data record infant birth weight in grams and mother's race (white, black, other). We label the numeric race codes and set <strong>white</strong> as reference.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: birthwt, white reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
data(birthwt)

birthwt <- birthwt |>
  mutate(race = factor(race, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                       labels = c("white", "black", "other")))

mod_race <- lm(bwt ~ race, data = birthwt)
summary(mod_race)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 6</div>
  <p>With white as reference, the intercept (about 3103 g) is the mean birth weight for:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="a">White mothers' babies.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="b">Black mothers' babies.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="c">All babies combined.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. White is the reference level." data-incorrect="Not quite. The intercept is the reference group mean."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 7</div>
  <p>The <code>raceblack</code> coefficient is about −383 g. The predicted mean birth weight for black mothers' babies is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="a">383 g</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="b">2720 g (3103 − 383)</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="c">3486 g (3103 + 383)</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Black mean = intercept + raceblack ≈ 3103 − 383 ≈ 2720 g." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the black coefficient to the intercept. The negative sign means lower than white."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Choosing the order and reference level</h2>

The first factor level is the <strong>reference</strong>. Choose the level order to match how you want to read the model output:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Natural order</strong>: lowest dose level, so effects read as changes from the low-dose group.</li>
  <li><strong>Outcome order</strong>: group levels ordered from lowest to highest outcome mean, so coefficients read as increases from the lowest group.</li>
  <li><strong>Clinical control</strong>: placebo or standard care, so every coefficient is a treatment effect.</li>
  <li><strong>Largest group</strong>: can yield tighter confidence intervals because the reference mean is estimated precisely.</li>
</ul>

For <code>birthwt</code>, the mean birth weights are lowest for black mothers' babies, then other, then white. Reorder <code>race</code> in that sequence and compare the output.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: order race by mean birth weight</h3>

```{webr-r}
birthwt_ordered <- birthwt |>
  mutate(race = factor(race, levels = c("black", "other", "white")))

mod_race_ordered <- lm(bwt ~ race, data = birthwt_ordered)
summary(mod_race_ordered)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 8</div>
  <p>With black as reference, the coefficient on <code>racewhite</code> is about +383 g. This means:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="a">White babies weigh about 383 g more than black babies, on average.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="b">White babies weigh 383 g in total.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="c">The race difference disappeared after reordering.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Same underlying gap, new order: white vs black instead of black vs white." data-incorrect="Not quite. Reordering factor levels relabels comparisons; it does not change the data or erase differences."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 9</div>
  <p>With black as reference, the intercept (about 2720 g) represents:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="a">The grand mean across all races.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="b">The white group mean.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="c">The black group mean.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The intercept always tracks the reference group." data-incorrect="Not quite. After reordering, black is first and is the reference, so the intercept is the black mean."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 1: plant weight by treatment (<code>PlantGrowth</code>)</h2>

The <code>PlantGrowth</code> data record dried plant weight (<code>weight</code>) for a control group and two treatment groups (<code>group</code>: ctrl, trt1, trt2). Fit a model with <code>weight</code> as the outcome and <code>group</code> as the predictor.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: exercise 1 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
data(PlantGrowth)

mod_plant <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = PlantGrowth)
summary(mod_plant)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
mod_plant <- lm(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
summary(mod_plant)
```

</details>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 10</div>
  <p>From your completed model, the predicted mean plant weight for <strong>trt2</strong> is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="a">0.49 units (the coefficient only).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="b">5.53 units (5.03 + 0.49).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="c">4.66 units (5.03 − 0.37).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The trt2 mean = intercept + grouptrt2 ≈ 5.03 + 0.49 ≈ 5.53." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the trt2 coefficient to the intercept. The coefficient is a difference from the control group."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 2: six-level spray predictor (<code>InsectSprays</code>)</h2>

The <code>InsectSprays</code> data record insect counts after different spray treatments. Fit a model with insect count (<code>count</code>) as the outcome and spray type (<code>spray</code>: A to F) as the predictor.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: exercise 2 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
data(InsectSprays)

mod_spray <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = InsectSprays)
summary(mod_spray)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
mod_spray <- lm(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)
```

With spray A as the default reference, the intercept is the mean count for spray A. Each other row is the difference vs spray A.

</details>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 11</div>
  <p>In the model <code>lm(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)</code>, how many spray coefficients appear below the intercept?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="a">5 (for B to F; A is reference).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="b">6 (one per spray).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="c">1 (spray is binary).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Six levels → five dummy variables (K − 1)." data-incorrect="Not quite. With K = 6 levels, expect K − 1 = 5 slope rows."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 12</div>
  <p>The <code>sprayC</code> coefficient (about −12.4) tells you that spray C's mean insect count is about 12.4:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="a">In total, regardless of spray type.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="b">Lower than the spray A reference group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="c">Lower than spray B specifically.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Each dummy compares its level to the reference (spray A), not to another non-reference level." data-incorrect="Not quite. The sprayC row is spray C vs spray A (reference), not spray C vs spray B."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel completion">

<h2>Completion code</h2>

<p>Answer at least 10 out of 12 questions correctly to reveal your completion code.</p>

<p><span class="code-progress" id="code-progress">0 of 12 correct (need at least 10)</span></p>

<div class="code-box" id="code-box">
  <div class="code-label">Your completion code</div>
  <div class="code-value" id="code-value"></div>
</div>

</section>

<p class="footer-note">GRAPH Courses practical | Polytomous categorical predictors</p>

</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "POLYKM1";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 10;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
